transcript:

Agent: Rahul ji, aapka account hamara paas hai. Aapke August ka EMI abhi tak clear nahi hua hai. Outstanding amount 18,500 rupees hai. Aap kab payment kar sakte ho?

Customer: Haan, main janta hoon, lekin abhi bilkul timing galat hai bhai. Meri maa ko accident ho gaya ek hafte pehle. Woh hospital mein admit hai.

Agent: Achcha... oh, I'm very sorry to hear that. Kya woh theek ho rahe hain?

Customer: Bilkul nahi. Uska ek foot fracture ho gaya aur spinal injury bhi hai. Doctors ne kaha hai ki kam se kam 2-3 mahine recovery lene honge. ICU mein tha, ab general ward mein hai. Lekin daily 15,000 se 20,000 tak hospital bills aa rahe hain. Meri savings bilkul khatam ho gayi.

Agent: Samajhta hoon, yeh bahut difficult situation hai. Aapka parivaar aur maa dono ki care ke liye paisa chahiye. Lekin Rahul, aapka August ka EMI abhi overdue hai. Aapne last month kya kiya tha?

Customer: Last month main ne try kiya tha, lekin maa ke accident ke baad sab kuch <interruption> sab kuch upar neeche ho gaya. Main ne July ka EMI to kiya tha, lekin August... August mein accident hua aur phir sab payment ruk gaya. Abhi to main apne aap ko sambhaal nahi paa raha hoon.

Agent: Bilkul, yeh samajh mein aa raha hai. Toh bataiye, aapka monthly income kitna hai?

Customer: Main IT field mein kaam karta hoon, aur mera base salary 55,000 rupees hai. Lekin abhi unpaid leave le rakha hai kyunki maa ke paas rehna padh raha hai. Toh abhi income zero hai practically. Mere pas jo savings the woh sab hospital mein chali gayi.

Agent: Achcha, samajhta hoon. Toh aapke paas abhi koi payment possible nahi hai?

Customer: Bilkul nahi, bhaiiya. Abhi to main bas apne aap ko theek karne ke liye koshish kar raha hoon. Aapka EMI to zaroor dena hai, lekin abhi nahi kar sakta. Maa ke liye paise chahiye. Kya aap kuch extension de sakte ho? Ek mahina ka time dedo. Shayad tab tak maa hospital se discharge ho jaaye aur main wapas kaam pe jaa saku.

Agent: Rahul, main samajhta hoon ki aapki situation bahut critical hai. Lekin mujhe batana padega ki aapka loan 18 din se overdue hai. Agar aap abhi kuch nahi karoge, to aapka account further deteriorate hoga. Aapka credit score bhi kharab hoga.

Customer: Bhai, credit score se mujhe abhi farak nahi padta. Mere maa ki jaan important hai. Agar aap samajhte ho to mujhe kuch time de do. Main apne manager se baat karunga aur dekhunga ki unpaid leave ke baad main kab wapas aa sakta hoon. Shayad do-teen hafte mein.

Agent: Theek hai, Rahul. Mujhe aapka situation samajh aa gaya. Aapka maa ka health hi sabse important hai. Lekin main aapko yeh bolna padega ki aapko formal hardship application dena padega. Isme aap apna medical situation explain kar sakte ho. Aur haan, jab aap wapas kaam pe aa jaao, to aap pehle July ka kharche wapas karo, phir August aur new charges ke saath.

Customer: Haan, woh application aap bhej do. Mujhe fill kar denge. Lekin main ek cheez aur poochtna chahta hoon - kya interest charges abhi bhi lag rahe hain? Kyunki agar har din interest badh raha hai, to mera balance to ek mahine mein double ho jayega.

Agent: Woh interest to default charges ke saath hi lag rahe hain, Rahul. Lekin jab aap hardship form submit karo, to uske baad aapke case ko review kiya jayega. Agar aapki situation verified ho, to possible hai ki interest ko hold kiya jaye ya kum kiya jaye. Lekin abhi main guarantee nahi de sakta.

Customer: Achcha theek hai. Toh mujhe kya karna chahiye ab?

Agent: Rahul, aap mujhe ek chiz do. Aapka hospital address bhi bata do jahan aapka maa admit hai. Aur ek baat - kya aap apne manager se hospital letter le sakte ho jisme likha ho ki aapne unpaid leave liya hai aur kab tak recovery period hoga?

Customer: Haan, main ek letter le lunga. Lekin hospital address... woh Fortis Hospital, Delhi mein hai. Mera number same hai - 98765-43210. Aur bataiye, mere liye kya timeline hai? Kab tak mujhe payment karna hoga?

Agent: Theek hai. Toh aap jab recover ho jaao aur wapas kaam pe jao, tab aap mujhe call karna. Aapka hardship form ke saath jo documents hain - medical bills, hospital discharge papers, aur company ka leave letter - sab bhej dena. Hum tab aapke case ko reassess karenge. Abhi ke liye, main aapka account ko 45 din ke liye hold kar dunga, lekin aapko call karte rahna padega agar koi update ho.

Customer: Bilkul, main call kar dunga. Lekin ek baat aur - kya mujhe kisi settlement ke baare mein bhi sochna chahiye? Agar main ek lump sum doon, to kya interest maaf ho jayega?

Agent: Rahul, abhi settlement ki baat mat karo. Pehle aapka situation stable ho, maa theek ho, phir dekhenge. Abhi to bas hardship form bhej do aur medical documents gather karo. Hum aapka case sympathetically handle karenge.

Customer: Theek hai, shukriya. Mujhe hope hai ki aapka lender samajhega. Maa ko recover hote hi main aapko call karunga.

Agent: Bilkul, Rahul. Aapka maa jaldi theek ho jaye, yeh meri duaa hai. Document bhej dena jab ready ho. Aur kisi bhi emergency ke liye directly mujhe call kar sakte ho. Take care.

Customer: Shukriya, bhaiiya. Aapne samajha, isliye acha laga. Goodbye.

transcript:
Agent: Hello, am I speaking with Rajesh Kumar?

Customer: Yes, speaking. Who is this?

Agent: Hi Rajesh, this is Priya calling from Quick Credit Finance regarding your loan account. How are you doing today?

Customer: Haan, I'm okay. But I know why you're calling. Look, I'm not avoiding anything. I want to clear this.

Agent: That's great to hear, Rajesh. So I have your account here — loan number QL-2847956. Outstanding balance is showing as 47,500 rupees, and the due date was the 15th of this month. It's now the 22nd. Can you tell me what's happening with the payment?

Customer: See, the thing is, my salary... my salary hasn't come yet. It was supposed to come on the 18th, but the company, they're saying there's some delay in processing this month. Some payroll system issue or something.

Agent: I understand. When are you expecting it to arrive? Do you have a confirmed date from your HR?

Customer: They told me it should be by the 25th, maximum. Definitely by the 25th. I've asked them twice already. Once that money comes in, first thing I'm doing is clearing your payment.

Agent: Okay, so by the 25th. But Rajesh, I need to ask — when the salary comes, will you have 47,500 available for this? Because sometimes salary comes but there are other expenses, other bills...

Customer: No, no, this is priority. I understand the situation. I've already made the commitment to clear this first. My wife knows too — she knows this payment has to go through. So once the salary hits, within a day or two maximum, you'll have the money.

Agent: That's very good to hear. And just to confirm, you're willing to make the full payment of 47,500 rupees by the 27th at the latest?

Customer: <interruption> Yes, yes, by the 27th. But... actually, can I ask you something?

Agent: Of course.

Customer: Is there any chance the interest or something has been calculated wrong? Because when I took the loan, it was supposed to be around 45,000 only, and I've already paid some amount earlier, no? So shouldn't the balance be less?

Agent: Let me check your payment history here. Okay, so you took the loan for 50,000 rupees. You've made two payments — one of 1,500 in August and one of 1,000 in September. So the calculation is correct. The balance after your payments is indeed 47,500.

Customer: Hmm, okay. But the interest charges seem quite high, yaar. I'm not disputing the amount, but just... it seems like a lot.

Agent: I understand your concern, Rajesh. Those are the interest charges as per your loan agreement. But the good news is, once you make the full payment by the 27th, no further interest will accrue. So it's in your interest to clear it as soon as the salary comes.

Customer: Yes, yes, I know. Okay, so I'm confirming — by the 27th of this month, you will get the full 47,500. Once my salary comes on the 25th, I'll transfer it immediately.

Agent: Perfect. So let me log this down. You're committing to a full payment of 47,500 rupees by September 27th, pending your salary credit on the 25th. Is that correct?

Customer: That's correct. But just make sure you don't call me too much between now and then, okay? One or two calls to remind me is fine, but not every day.

Agent: Understood, Rajesh. I'll schedule a courtesy reminder call for the 26th, just to confirm the salary has arrived. Does that work?

Customer: Yes, that's fine. The 26th is good.

Agent: Thank you for your commitment, Rajesh. I'm logging this as a Promise to Pay for the 27th. You have my assurance that we won't harass you. Just get that salary in and make the payment. Is there anything else you need from me today?

Customer: No, that's it. I appreciate your understanding. I'll make sure it's done.

Agent: Great. All the best, Rajesh. We'll speak on the 26th then.

Customer: Okay, thanks. Bye.

Agent: Bye, Rajesh.

Customer: Everything is... it's fine. Or not fine. I don't know anymore, actually. The money is there, I think. Or maybe it's not. My wife usually handles this, but she's... she's upset with me right now. We had a big fight yesterday.

Agent: I understand, sir. These things happen. But we do need to get the payment sorted. When do you think you might be able to arrange it?

Customer: I don't know. I really don't know. Some days I feel like everything is falling apart, you know? The loan, the house, my marriage... sometimes I just don't see the point of paying anything. Why should I even try?

Agent: Sir, I can hear that you're going through something difficult. Are you okay? Is there something else troubling you besides the payment?

Customer: <interruption> No, no, I'm fine. I'm fine. It's just... I haven't been sleeping well. And my boss, he's been very demanding lately. I feel like my head is going to explode. Sometimes I think about... I think about just leaving everything behind. Running away or... or worse.

Agent: Sir, I'm genuinely concerned about what you're saying. Have you spoken to anyone about how you're feeling? A doctor or someone you trust?

Customer: A doctor? No. Why would I do that? I'm not crazy. I'm just tired. So tired. The loan payment... yes, I can probably pay it next week when my salary comes. Or maybe the week after. I'm not sure when the salary will come anymore. My company is having problems too.

Agent: Sir, I appreciate you sharing this with me. The payment is important, but right now I'm more concerned about you. Do you have someone you can talk to? Family, a friend, or a professional?

Customer: I... I don't know. My wife won't listen. My parents are old, I don't want to burden them. And my friends, they all think I'm doing fine. I can't tell them that I'm not. That I'm just... empty inside.

Agent: Sir, please listen to me. What you're describing sounds very serious. I want to help, but not with the payment right now. Have you heard of AASRA or iCall? They're helplines for people going through what you're going going through. Would you like me to give you a number?

Customer: <interruption> I... maybe. I don't know. This is strange. You're a collection agent. Why are you asking me this?

Agent: Because you matter more than this loan right now, sir. Your wellbeing is more important. I'm going to pause all collection activity on your account. I'm flagging this for our specialist team who are trained to help people in situations like yours. They will reach out to you, but only to see how you're doing, not to demand payment. Is that okay?

Customer: Okay. I... yes. That's okay. I think I need help. I didn't think anyone would ask.

Agent: You did the right thing by being honest with me. I'm going to make sure your account is marked as requiring specialist support. Please reach out to AASRA at 9820466726 or iCall at 9152987821. They're available 24/7. Will you call them?

Customer: I'll try. I think I will. Thank you. I wasn't expecting this.

Customer: <pause> Okay, I'm back. Sorry about that. Look, Priya, the situation is very complicated right now. You see, I run a small textile business in Surat, and there was this massive flood in the city last month. The entire warehouse... everything got destroyed. Literally everything.

Customer: The monsoon rain was extremely heavy, and the water came into our warehouse at night. We didn't even know until morning. By that time, all the raw materials, finished stock, everything was soaked. We lost almost two months of inventory, which is about fifteen to twenty lakhs of rupees worth of goods. The insurance claim is still pending, and the assessor only came two weeks back.

Agent: That's a significant loss, Rajesh. I'm sorry to hear that. And your business operations... are you able to continue working?

Customer: That's the problem, Priya. We had to shut down for almost three weeks because we had no stock to work with. Even now, we are running at maybe thirty percent capacity. I had to take loans from relatives just to restart some operations and pay my workers' salaries. The business income has dropped to almost nothing compared to before. That's why I couldn't pay the EMI on the 15th.

Agent: I see. So the flood has directly impacted your business cash flow. Have you been able to make any partial payment since the due date?

Customer: No, nothing yet. I have been using every rupee to pay my workers and to buy even basic materials to restart. My bank account is running on empty, Priya. I am not refusing to pay you, but I literally cannot pay right now. The insurance claim should come through in the next two or three weeks, and once that happens, I will be able to clear everything, including the arrears.

Agent: Rajesh, I appreciate you explaining the situation. Can I confirm a few details? What is your current business address? Is it still in Surat?

Customer: Yes, yes, same location. But the warehouse itself is damaged and unusable. We are operating from a small rented space temporarily while the repairs are happening. The address is... let me think... it's Plot Number 42, Textile Park Extension, near Kadodara. But I'm staying at my home address most days now. You have my home address in the file, correct?

Agent: Yes, we have your residential address on file. And Rajesh, when you say the insurance claim should come in two to three weeks, is that a confirmed timeline from the insurance company?

Customer: The assessor visited and said the report would be ready within ten to twelve days. After that, it goes for approval, which should be another week or so. So yes, hopefully by end of next month, definitely by mid-month at the latest.

Agent: Understood. And Rajesh, just to clarify — this is a temporary situation caused by the flood, correct? Once the insurance payout comes through, your business and your ability to pay should recover?

Customer: Yes, yes, exactly. This is not a permanent problem. My business was doing well before the flood. Once I restart with new stock and the insurance money comes, everything will be normal again. I am not a defaulter by nature, Priya. This is just bad timing, bad luck.

Agent: I believe you, Rajesh. Given what you've described, we would like to help you through this difficult period. Let me escalate this to our hardship team. In the meantime, can you commit to making the payment once your insurance claim is processed? And do you have any amount you can pay in the next week or two, even as a partial payment?

Customer: I wish I could, but honestly, I don't have anything right now. Every rupee is committed. But once the insurance comes through, I will pay the full amount plus the arrears immediately. You have my word. And yes, please escalate it. I want to settle this properly.

Agent: Of course, Rajesh. We understand that life sometimes throws unexpected challenges at us. Our job is to work with you, not against you. We'll be in touch shortly. Take care.

Customer: Thank you, Priya. I appreciate it very much. I will wait for their call.

transcript:
Agent: Good morning, am I speaking to Rajesh Kumar? This is Priya from the collections team at Fintech Solutions.

Customer: Haan, yes, speaking. But look, I... I'm not in a good position right now to talk about payment, yaar.

Agent: I understand, Rajesh. I'm calling regarding your loan account ending in 4827. You have an outstanding balance of Rs. 1,84,000 and your EMI was due on the 15th of this month. It's now the 22nd. Can we discuss your payment plan?

Customer: See, the thing is... <interruption> my company, they shut down operations last month. Completely shut down. I was working as a senior executive there for eight years, and suddenly they... they just closed everything down. No notice, nothing proper.

Agent: Oh, I see. So you've recently lost your job?

Customer: Yes, lost my job. And my salary for last month? Still pending. The management says they have cash flow issues, so they cannot release salaries. Already two months without proper income, Priya. My wife is asking me every day how we will manage the kids' school fees, the house rent...

Agent: I'm sorry to hear that, Rajesh. This is a difficult situation. But let me ask you — do you have any savings or alternate source of income right now?

Customer: Savings? Haan, I have some, maybe Rs. 30,000 or 40,000 in the bank, but that's for emergency. If I use that for your loan, what will I do for the next month? My wife's salary is only Rs. 25,000, and that goes to rent and school fees and groceries. Everything is stretched, you understand?

Agent: Yes, I understand. Have you been looking for another job?

Customer: Of course I'm looking! I've sent out maybe 50 resumes in the last month. I have two interviews lined up next week, but nothing confirmed yet. And even if I get a job, there's a notice period — at least 30 days before I start earning again. So realistically, I'm looking at maybe two months before I can start making payments again.

Agent: Okay, Rajesh. So you're facing a temporary income disruption due to the job loss. Have you considered approaching the previous employer or their creditors for the outstanding salary?

Customer: I tried! The management office is basically shut. The owner is not responding to calls. I went there personally yesterday — the office is locked. It's a mess.

Agent: I see. And your wife's income of Rs. 25,000 — that's really just covering your basic expenses?

Customer: Exactly. Rent is Rs. 18,000, school fees are Rs. 5,000, groceries maybe Rs. 3,000, utilities... by the time we pay everything, there's nothing left. Your EMI of Rs. 18,000 — where am I supposed to get that from right now?

Agent: I understand, Rajesh. This is a genuine hardship case. Let me be honest with you — based on what you've told me, your income has been disrupted and you don't have the capacity to pay the full EMI right now. But I need to ask: do you have any other loans or EMIs you're paying?

Customer: Yes, there's a home loan. That's Rs. 12,000 per month. So between your EMI and the home loan, it's Rs. 30,000. My wife's salary is Rs. 25,000. You tell me how I manage?

Agent: That's a real squeeze. So you're overextended even before the job loss. Rajesh, I want to help you here. What I'm going to do is escalate your account for a hardship assessment. We can look at options like a temporary moratorium or restructuring your EMI, but I need to verify your situation first. Can you provide me with documentation — your termination letter, your wife's salary slip, and any correspondence from your previous employer about the pending salary?

Customer: I have the termination letter. I have my wife's salary slips from the last three months. As for the employer, I don't have anything in writing — they just stopped coming to the office. I can get you whatever else you need, but it will take a few days.

Agent: That's fine. Send me the termination letter and your wife's last three salary slips. Once I have that, I'll escalate this to our hardship team. In the meantime, Rajesh, can you commit to paying something — even a partial amount — in the next 10 days? Maybe Rs. 10,000 or 15,000 from your savings, just to show good faith?

Customer: Priya, I really can't spare that right now. If I do that, I won't be able to pay the rent by the end of the month. I'm not refusing to pay you — I'm telling you I genuinely cannot right now. But once I get a job or once the previous company pays my pending salary, I promise I will clear this. I just need some time.

Agent: I hear you, Rajesh. I'm not going to pressure you for a payment you can't make. What I'll do is flag your account for a 60-day hardship moratorium pending documentation. This means no late fees will accrue for the next 60 days while we assess your situation. But I need you to send those documents within the next three days — termination letter and salary slips. Can you do that?

Customer: Yes, yes, I can do that. I'll send them by email tomorrow or day after. Thank you for understanding.

Agent: You're welcome. And Rajesh, if your situation improves before the 60 days — if you get a job or receive your pending salary — please let me know immediately. We can revisit the moratorium and work out a payment plan. For now, my colleague will send you an email with the documentation requirements and the email address where you can submit them. Okay?

Customer: Okay, thank you. I appreciate this. I was worried you'd just keep pressuring me like the last agent did.

Agent: No, that's not how we operate in hardship cases. Take care, Rajesh. We'll be in touch after we receive your documents.
L3: Hardship – Job Loss / Income Disruption|Overindebtedness – Other Lender EMI Competing Priority|Identity Confirmed – Borrower Verified on Call|Commitment Conditional – Subject to External Factor|Salary Delayed – Awaiting Credit

transcript:
Agent: Good afternoon, may I speak with Rajesh Kumar, please?

Customer: Yes, this is Rajesh speaking. Who is this?

Agent: Hello Rajesh, this is Priya from the collections team at FinServe Credit. I'm calling regarding your personal loan account ending in 4782. Do you have a couple of minutes to speak with me?

Customer: Haan, haan, I know about this. Look, I've been meaning to call you people. My EMI is due on the 15th, right? Twelve thousand five hundred rupees every month?

Agent: Yes, that's correct. Your EMI of twelve thousand five hundred is due on the 15th of every month. I'm calling because your account is currently thirty days overdue. The last payment we received was on the 28th of August. Rajesh, can you help me understand what's happened since then?

Customer: See, the thing is... <interruption> sorry, sorry. My business was doing okay until about three months back. Then one of my major clients just stopped placing orders. I mean, completely stopped. And my wife, she also lost her job around the same time. So now we're... we're managing on just my reduced income from what little work I'm getting.

Agent: I understand, Rajesh. That sounds like a very difficult situation. So you're facing an income disruption right now. Apart from this FinServe loan, do you have any other EMIs or loan obligations?

Customer: Yes, yes. There's a housing loan with HDFC Bank, around eighteen thousand per month, and a bike loan with another NBFC for about four thousand. So in total, I'm looking at almost thirty-four thousand in EMIs every month. But my income now is maybe... maybe twenty-five to twenty-six thousand on average. I'm falling short every month.

Agent: That's a significant gap, Rajesh. So you're in a position where your monthly EMI obligations are exceeding your current income. And that's why the FinServe EMI has slipped?

Customer: Exactly. I've been prioritizing the housing loan because, you know, if I default there, they can take the house. The bike loan I've been managing somehow. But your EMI... I just didn't have the money. I know I owe it, I'm not denying that. I just... I can't pay the full amount right now.

Agent: I hear you. And I appreciate your honesty, Rajesh. Now, you mentioned you can't pay the full amount. What would be possible for you right now? Can you make a partial payment towards this outstanding amount?

Customer: <interruption> Maybe I can find two or three thousand, but that's not going to solve the problem, is it? Because next month I'll be in the same situation. And the month after that. It's not a one-time thing. I need some kind of... I don't know, maybe reduce my EMI? Or extend the loan period so the monthly payment comes down? That's the only way I can manage this.

Agent: That's a fair point. So you're looking for some restructuring of the loan terms. Let me note that down. You're asking for either a reduction in your monthly EMI or an extension of the loan tenure to bring the monthly payment down to a level you can manage. Is that correct?

Customer: Yes, exactly. Or even a moratorium for a few months? Like, can you give me three or four months where I don't have to pay, and then resume? My business might pick up by then. One of my old clients is supposed to get back to me in October.

Agent: I understand, Rajesh. A moratorium or payment holiday is another option. So you're looking at relief measures — either an EMI reduction, a tenure extension, a payment holiday, or some combination of these — so that your monthly obligation aligns with your current income. Is that fair to say?

Customer: Haan, that's exactly what I'm saying. I want to pay, but I need breathing room. I can't pay twelve thousand five hundred right now, but if it comes down to maybe seven or eight thousand, I can manage that from my current income.

Agent: Rajesh, I want to be very clear about this. What you're requesting is a legitimate request, and it's something we can escalate to our senior team for assessment. However, I need to manage your expectations. We cannot promise a restructure or a moratorium on this call. What I can do is document your request, escalate it to our loan management team, and they will review your situation — your income documents, your current obligations, your hardship circumstances — and then they will reach out to you with a decision.

Customer: How long will that take? And what do I do about this thirty-day overdue status in the meantime?

Agent: That's a good question. Once we escalate, the team typically reviews within seven to ten working days. During that time, your account will be flagged as under review for restructure, and standard collection activity will be paused. It won't make the overdue status disappear, but it gives us time to assess the situation properly.

Agent: Hello, is this Vikram Sharma? This is Deepika calling from Finserve Collections. I'm reaching out regarding your loan account number ending in 7634, outstanding balance of 52,800 rupees.

Customer: Haan, haan, Vikram here. But listen, I don't understand why you're calling. This loan, yaar, it was cancelled before the money was even given to me. I applied for the loan, but then I got the job confirmed at TCS, so I called the bank immediately and told them — don't disburse, don't disburse. They said okay, we'll cancel it. Toh yeh account should not even exist in your system, na?

Agent: <interruption> Sir, I understand. Can you tell me approximately when this happened? Which month?

Customer: It was in March, last year. March 2023 I applied, within two weeks I got my new job offer, and I immediately called their loan processing team and said cancel karo. They confirmed cancellation over the phone. Then in April I got the official letter — "Loan Application Cancelled, No Disbursement Made." Everything was finished, na. So I don't know why this outstanding balance is showing now.

Agent: Sir, I appreciate you sharing this. But here's the thing — our system still shows this account as active with 52,800 rupees outstanding. Now, this could mean either the cancellation letter you received was for a different loan application, or there's been a processing error on our end. Can you describe what the cancellation letter said exactly?

Customer: It said "Loan Application Status: Cancelled Before Disbursement. No funds have been credited to your account. No further action required." Bilkul clear likha tha. I have that letter at home. Why would I keep it if it wasn't real, haan? And I never received any money in my account, never made a single payment — nothing. So how can there be an outstanding balance on a loan that was never disbursed?

Agent: <interruption> That's a very fair point, sir. Let me check something in our system. When you applied for this loan, what was the exact amount you had applied for?

Customer: It was 1 lakh 50 thousand rupees. For a bike, actually. But then the job offer came, and I didn't need the bike anymore, so I cancelled. Very simple, na. No loan, no money, no dues.

Agent: Sir, I completely understand your frustration. But I'm seeing here that the account shows a first disbursement of 1,50,000 rupees in March 2023, and then a payment of 97,200 rupees in April. So it appears the loan was actually disbursed, and a partial payment was made. This contradicts the cancellation claim. Can you explain this?

Customer: <pause> Wait, what? 97,200? I never made any payment. That's... that's not possible. Unless... <interruption> oh, I remember now. My father, he took some money from his savings and put it into my account in April. He gave me 97,200 for some other purpose. But that was not a loan payment — that was just him helping me out. And I never asked for the loan to be disbursed in the first place. Maybe they processed it without my consent after I cancelled?

Agent: Okay, sir. So you're saying you didn't authorise the disbursement after you requested cancellation?

Customer: Exactly! I called and said cancel, they said okay. Then why would they disburse? That's fraud, na. They took my application and disbursed without my permission. Then my father put money in my account, and they probably took that as a payment. But I never agreed to this loan being active. It was cancelled before disbursement — that's what their letter said.

Agent: Sir, I hear you. But the letter you're referring to — it says "Cancelled Before Disbursement," but our records show a disbursement happened. So either the letter was issued in error, or there's a mismatch between what you requested and what actually processed. This is definitely something we need to investigate. Do you still have that cancellation letter with you?

Customer: Haan, it's somewhere at home. I can look for it. But even if I find it, what difference does it make? You're telling me your own system shows the disbursement happened after the cancellation letter was issued. So your bank made the error, not me. I should not be held liable for your mistake, haan? I cancelled the loan. I have the letter. Case closed.

Agent: You're right, sir, and I'm not saying this is your fault. But to resolve this properly, I do need to see that cancellation letter. Can you email it to us, or would you prefer to visit a branch? Once we match it against our records, we can investigate the disbursement discrepancy and take appropriate action. The email is collections-disputes@finserve.co.in.

Customer: Email kaise? I don't have a scanner at home. And which branch? I'm in Pune now, I work near Hinjewadi. The nearest Finserve branch is in Kalyani Nagar, and it's quite far. I can't take time out for this. Your mistake, your responsibility to fix it, na?

Agent: <interruption> Sir, I completely understand. You don't need a scanner — you can use your phone camera to take a photo of the letter and email it. Or if you prefer, I can arrange for our field team to visit you at your address and collect the document. Which would be easier for you?

Customer: <pause> Okay, fine. I'll take a photo and email it. But I'm telling you, this should have been resolved a year ago. You disbursed without my permission, then your system showed it as outstanding. This is your mess, not mine. I'll send the letter, but I'm not responsible for any of this.

Agent: Absolutely, sir. I'm noting your claim that the loan was cancelled before disbursement and that you have documentary evidence. I'm creating a dispute flag on your account right now. Once you email the letter, we'll investigate within 48 hours. In the meantime, I'm placing a "Do Not Call" hold on your account. You won't hear from us until we've reviewed the documents. Can I have your email address to send you confirmation?

Customer: vikram.sharma.pune@gmail.com. And please, no more calls until you've sorted this out, okay? I've wasted enough time on this already.

Agent: Noted, sir. vikram.sharma.pune@gmail.com. You have a good day, and thank you for your patience.

Customer: Okay, goodbye.

Agent: Hello, am I speaking with Mr. Rajesh Kumar?

Customer: Haan, yes, this is Rajesh. Who is calling?

Customer: Yes yes, I know why you are calling. Look, I can explain the situation. It's not that I don't want to pay. Things have become very difficult suddenly.

Agent: I understand, Mr. Kumar. Your outstanding balance is currently Rs. 1,87,450 and your EMI of Rs. 8,900 is now 16 days overdue. Can you tell me what is happening on your end? What is the difficulty you are facing?

Customer: <interruption> The problem is, my company... I was working at Precision Engineering for the last seven years, and two weeks ago they closed down the entire division. Just like that. No warning, no notice period. They told us to leave by Friday.

Agent: Oh, I see. That must be very stressful, Mr. Kumar. So you have lost your job recently?

Customer: Yes, lost my job. And I have been doing interviews since then, but nothing is confirmed yet. I have a family to support — my wife, two children. My wife does some part-time teaching work, but it's only about 12,000 rupees per month. That is not enough to cover everything — the house rent, the children's school fees, and now this EMI.

Agent: I completely understand, sir. This is a difficult situation. Tell me, do you have any savings or liquid funds right now that we could use to make at least a partial payment towards this EMI?

Customer: <interruption> Partial? No, no, I don't have even that much right now. I had to use my savings to pay the house rent for last month. I was hoping... I thought maybe I could get a new job within a week or two, and then I could clear the full amount. But it's been two weeks already and nothing has come through. My previous company is also not giving me any severance or dues because of the sudden closure.

Agent: I see, Mr. Kumar. I appreciate you being honest about this. Let me explain what options we have. First, I need to understand — when you were employed, what was your monthly salary?

Customer: I was earning about 65,000 rupees per month, plus some bonuses. So roughly 70 to 75 thousand some months. Now my wife's income is only 12,000. How can I pay 8,900 rupees EMI on just 12,000 rupees? And we still need to eat, pay rent...

Agent: Yes, that is a significant drop in household income. Mr. Kumar, given this situation, I would like to escalate your case for a hardship assessment. This could potentially lead to a moratorium or restructuring of your loan for a few months until you find employment. But I need some more information. What is your expected timeline to find a new job?

Customer: I don't know, honestly. I have applied to maybe five or six companies. Some said they will call me in two weeks, some in a month. My friend told me there might be something in his company, but that is not confirmed. I could be looking at one month, maybe two months before I get something stable.

Agent: Understood. And during this period, can you commit to making any payment at all? Even a small amount, just to show good faith?

Customer: <interruption> Look, I cannot promise anything right now. I am barely managing to keep food on the table. Next month, if I get a job, then yes, I can pay something. But asking me to pay now... it's just not possible. I am not refusing because I don't want to — I literally don't have the money.

Agent: I hear you, Mr. Kumar. This is not a refusal situation; this is a genuine hardship. Let me make a note here. I am going to escalate your case to our hardship team for a formal assessment. They will review your situation and may offer you options like a payment moratorium for two to three months, after which your EMIs can resume or be restructured. Is that something you would be interested in?

Customer: Yes, yes, that would help a lot. How long will this take? And what do I need to do?

Agent: The hardship team will contact you within the next 48 hours. They may ask for some documents — your previous salary slips, proof of job loss from your company, and your wife's income proof. Can you gather those?

Customer: Yes, I can try. I have my last three months of salary slips. For the job loss, my company gave me an email saying we are all terminated due to division closure. And my wife has her school letter showing her part-time work and salary.

Agent: Perfect, Mr. Kumar. That should be sufficient. Please keep those documents ready. One more thing — if you do manage to find any interim income or if you can make even a partial payment before the hardship team reaches out, please contact us immediately at this number. Can I confirm your contact number is still 9876543210?

Customer: Yes, that is correct.

Agent: Great. So to summarize: I am escalating your case for hardship assessment due to recent job loss and significant income disruption. The team will contact you within 48 hours. In the meantime, you do not need to worry about collection calls. Please gather the documents I mentioned. Is there anything else you would like me to note down before I close this call?

Customer: No, I think that's it. Thank you for understanding. I am not someone who runs away from my responsibilities. I will get back on my feet and pay this loan. It's just a temporary situation.

Agent: I completely understand, Mr. Kumar. We appreciate your honesty and willingness to work with us. Our hardship team will be in touch soon. Take care, and best of luck with your job search.

Customer: Thank you. Goodbye.

transcript:
Agent: Namaste, is this Rajesh Kumar? Rajesh Kumar Sharma?

Customer: Haan, haan, I am speaking. Who is this?

Agent: Sir, main Priya bol rahi hoon from Fintech Finance Limited. Aapke account ke baare mein ek call tha. Your account number 45782903 — do you recognise?

Customer: Haan, haan, I know, I know. But see, right now is not a good time. Mera sab kuch <interruption> — everything is messed up, yaar.

Agent: Sir, I understand, but this is very important. Your outstanding amount is 3,47,500 rupees. The due date was 10th September, and today is 28th. You have not made any payment yet. Can we discuss?

Customer: Priya, you don't understand. Last month, we had this massive flood. In Nashik, where my business is — textile manufacturing — everything got destroyed. The machinery, the raw materials, everything went into the water. The government, they are saying maybe some relief will come, but nothing yet. How can I pay when my entire workshop is underwater?

Agent: Oh, I see. I'm very sorry to hear that. When did this happen, sir?

Customer: It was 3rd September. Just one week before my payment was due. The rain came, the river overflowed, and — <interruption> — sorry, sorry. It's just very stressful. My workers are also asking for their wages. I cannot even pay them right now.

Agent: Sir, I completely understand your situation. This is a very serious matter. Can you tell me — do you have any documentation? Like from the local administration, or insurance, or anything showing the damage?

Customer: Haan, I have some photos. The municipal corporation also gave me a letter saying the area was affected. But that is not helping me right now. I am living in my brother's house in Pune for now. The workshop is closed. No production, no income. Zero. Bilkul zero.

Agent: I see, sir. And when do you think the situation might improve? When can you expect to restart?

Customer: The water is still there, yaar. The cleanup will take maybe one month, two months? And then I need to buy new machinery, new materials. The bank is also not giving me any new credit because of this. It's a complete disaster. My wife is asking me every day — kya hoga? What will happen? I don't know what to tell her.

Agent: Sir, I hear your concern. Let me tell you what we can do. Since this is an external event — a natural disaster — we have some options. We can request a payment holiday or moratorium for, let's say, two months. During this time, you won't have to pay the EMI. Can you provide us with the municipal letter and photos as documentation?

Customer: Really? You can do that? Because I was very worried. I thought they will send police or something. <interruption> But yes, yes, I can send you the photos and the letter. I have it on WhatsApp also. Can I send it to you?

Agent: Yes, sir, absolutely. You can send it to our collections team email, which I will give you. But sir, I need to ask — after the two-month moratorium, when you restart production, you will be able to resume the EMI payment, correct? This is just a temporary relief.

Customer: Yes, yes, of course. Once the workshop is running again, I will pay. I want to pay. I am not someone who runs away from debt. It's just... right now, there is nothing. The flood has taken everything.

Agent: I understand, sir. And I appreciate your honesty. Let me also ask — do you have any other loans active right now? With other banks or NBFCs?

Customer: Haan, there is one loan with HDFC for the workshop equipment. That is 1.5 lakh EMI every month. So you can imagine — with this one loan plus your EMI, it's very difficult. But I am managing that somehow by borrowing from my brother.

Agent: I see. So you are also facing some overindebtedness situation here. That is important information. Sir, I will escalate your case to our senior team. We will review the documentation you send, and we will consider a two-month moratorium. You should expect to hear from us within 3 to 4 working days. In the meantime, please send the municipal letter and photos to collections@fintechfinance.in. Can you do that?

Customer: Yes, yes, I will send today itself. Priya, thank you. At least someone is listening. I was very scared.

Agent: No problem at all, sir. We are here to help. One more thing — during this moratorium period, when things stabilize, you will also need to think about how to restructure the payment. Maybe a longer tenure, or a reduced EMI. We can discuss that once you restart. For now, let's just get the documentation in.

Customer: Okay, okay. I will send it. Thank you, Priya. Thank you very much.

Agent: You're welcome, sir. And sir, please try to stay positive. These things happen. The important thing is you are communicating with us. That helps a lot. We will be in touch within 4 days. Take care.

Customer: Thank you. Bye.

Customer: Yes, yes. It says Apex Finance is taking some action, legal action. It's dated two weeks back. I didn't... I mean, I was planning to pay, but things got delayed, no? The amount they're showing, it's like Rs 3,47,500 or something. That seems very high to me. I paid regularly before, I think maybe 18 months back I paid something. After that my father got ill, the medical bills were too much, so I couldn't... I mean, I fell behind. But this interest they're charging, it's like double the original amount I borrowed, isn't it?

Agent: Vikram, I understand. Medical emergencies are difficult. Let me be clear about where we are now. Because legal proceedings have been initiated, this is no longer a standard collection call. I need to make sure you understand the seriousness. The outstanding balance as of today is Rs 3,47,520 including principal, accumulated interest, and processing fees. This case is currently being handled by our legal department. Before we discuss any resolution, I need to confirm some details for our records. Can you confirm your current residential address for me?

Customer: My address? It's the same as it was when I took the loan, no? Flat 7B, Shivaji Nagar, New Delhi. The one I gave you people at the beginning.

Agent: And that address is still current? You're living there now?

Customer: Yes, yes, I'm there. Same place. Why are you asking? Is there some problem?

Agent: No problem, Vikram. I'm just confirming for our file. Now, because this case is in the legal stage, I cannot directly settle or structure a payment with you on this call. Any resolution needs to be reviewed and approved by our legal team. However, I want to understand your situation first. You mentioned you were planning to pay. Are you in a position to make a payment now? Or is there a timeframe when you might be able to?

Customer: <interruption> Now? No, no, I don't have that kind of money sitting around right now. But... but my business has picked up a bit in the last two months. If I can get maybe three weeks, I might be able to arrange something. Not the full amount, but... maybe 1.5 lakhs? And then perhaps another payment after that?

Agent: Three weeks is a tight timeline, Vikram, especially now that legal action has started. Let me explain what happens next. I will document this call and your situation — your acknowledgement of the legal notice, your current inability to pay the full amount, and your indication that you might arrange a partial payment within three weeks. I will then escalate this entire case file, including everything you've just told me, to our legal team. They will review whether a settlement arrangement or payment plan is possible given the legal proceedings. They may contact you directly, or they may suggest we proceed with the case in court. This is now out of my hands. Do you understand?

Customer: Wait, wait. So you're saying the legal team will call me? They're the ones who decide if I can pay in parts?

Agent: Yes, exactly. The legal team will be the ones making the decision on how to proceed. They have authority to negotiate settlements or payment arrangements in cases like yours. I'm simply routing your file to them with all the details. You should expect contact from them within the next 48 hours, likely.

Customer: Okay, but... but I'm worried, no? What if they say no? What if they just take me to court anyway? My wife is very stressed about this. And the interest thing — I really don't think all of that interest is correct. The way they calculated it, it seems like they're charging me extra.

Agent: Those are concerns you can raise directly with the legal team when they contact you. They will have all the account details and can review the calculation with you. I'm noting in your file that you dispute the interest charged. That will be part of what gets escalated. But Vikram, I want to be clear: right now, because the legal notice has been issued, you're in a critical window. The legal team will be your best path forward. They have the authority to negotiate and find a solution. My job is to make sure they have all the information about your situation — which I do now.

Customer: Okay, okay. And you said they'll call in 48 hours? This number, right? <interruption> Or should I call them first?

Agent: No, don't call. Let them contact you. They have the case file now. They'll reach out. Just make sure this number stays active and you answer when they call. It's very important. Can you confirm this is still your active number — the one I'm calling right now?

Customer: Yes, this is my number. I always have it with me.

Agent: Good. So to recap: I'm escalating your file to the legal team right now. You've acknowledged the legal notice. You've indicated you may be able to arrange a partial payment within three weeks. You dispute the interest calculation. And I've confirmed your address as Flat 7B, Shivaji Nagar. The legal team will contact you within 48 hours to discuss next steps. Is there anything else I should note before I close this?

Customer: No, I think... I think that's it. I'm still worried, but at least someone will talk to me properly about this. Thank you for explaining.

Agent: You're welcome, Vikram. The legal team will be in touch. Keep your phone available. Take care.

Agent: Sir, this is Vikram from LendSmart Collections. I am calling regarding your loan account with us. Your reference number is LS-892456. Sir, your account is currently overdue by 47 days. The outstanding amount is rupees 1,34,500 and the payment was due on the 15th of this month. Do you have a few minutes to discuss this?

Customer: Haan, haan, I know about this. But sir, I have a problem right now. I actually want to pay, but... <interruption> sorry, I cannot pay right now because my bank account is frozen.

Agent: Frozen? What do you mean frozen, sir? Like, the account is blocked by the bank?

Customer: Yes, yes, exactly. The bank has put a hold on my account. I went to the branch yesterday and they told me that there is some regulatory issue or something. They said the account is under compliance review. I don't know exactly what happened, but I cannot withdraw or transfer any money from that account right now. It is completely blocked.

Agent: I see, sir. This is the HDFC account ending in 4521, correct?

Customer: Haan, that one only. My salary also comes in that account and I received it just three days back, but I cannot access it. The money is sitting there but I cannot touch it, yaar. It is very frustrating.

Agent: Understood, sir. So you are willing to pay, but the account is operationally blocked by the bank due to a compliance hold. Have they given you any timeline on when this freeze will be lifted?

Customer: No, no, they just said that it will take 5 to 7 working days. Maybe next week Tuesday or Wednesday it will be resolved. After that, I can withdraw and pay you immediately. I have the money, sir. The salary is there. I am not running away or anything like that.

Agent: That is good to know, sir. I appreciate your honesty. Now, sir, do you have any other bank account? Or maybe a savings account with another bank where you can transfer funds once the freeze is lifted? Or perhaps a co-applicant account that we can use?

Customer: No, sir. This HDFC account is my main account. I have an old ICICI account but that one I have not used in many years. I don't even remember if it is still active. My wife has an account, but that is a joint account and she is currently out of station. She is with her parents in Bangalore. So even that is not immediately available.

Agent: I understand. Sir, let me check if we can accept an alternate payment method in the interim. Can you make a payment via UPI once your account is unfrozen? Or would you prefer a bank transfer – NEFT or IMPS – once the hold is lifted?

Customer: UPI is better, sir. I use Google Pay and PhonePe regularly. Once the account is unfrozen, I can immediately do a UPI transfer. That will be faster, no?

Agent: Absolutely, sir. UPI is fastest. Now, sir, based on what you have told me, your account is operationally blocked until next Tuesday or Wednesday. I will make a note here that you are willing to pay the full outstanding amount of rupees 1,34,500 via UPI as soon as your account freeze is lifted. Is that correct?

Customer: Yes, yes, that is correct. But sir, one more thing – <interruption> sorry, the interest that has been charged... I received the SMS alert showing rupees 1,34,500, but I think that interest amount is too much. I had paid some amount three months back. Why is the interest so high?

Agent: Sir, that is a valid question. Let me pull up your payment history. <pause> I see here that you made a payment of rupees 28,000 on the 20th of June. After that, you have missed all EMI payments since July. So the interest has been accruing for the last 47 days. The calculation should be accurate, but if you feel there is an error, we can verify the full ledger and send it to you via email or SMS. Would you like me to do that?

Customer: Haan, send it to me. I want to see the breakdown. Maybe there is a processing fee or something that should not be there. But anyway, once my account is unfrozen, I will pay whatever is correct.

Agent: Perfect, sir. I will send the detailed ledger to your registered email within 2 hours. Now, sir, I am going to schedule a follow-up call for next Thursday at 3 PM. By that time, your account should be unfrozen and you will have the funds available. Is Thursday at 3 PM okay for you?

Customer: Haan, Thursday is fine. Actually, sir, I should have the account unfrozen by Wednesday evening itself. But calling on Thursday is safe. Let me just note down – Thursday at 3 PM. What is the number I should call back on if I manage to pay before Thursday?

Agent: Good question, sir. You can call me directly on 9876543210 or you can use the payment link that we will send you via SMS once your account is unfrozen. The link will have a UPI option. You can also reply to the SMS and let us know once you have made the payment. We will verify it on our end.

Customer: Okay, okay. So Thursday 3 PM is the scheduled call. I will try to pay before that if possible. And sir, one more request – can you please not call me before the account is unfrozen? I am already stressed because the account is blocked and I have a child who is very sensitive to phone calls. Just the Thursday follow-up is enough.

Agent: Absolutely, sir. I am noting down here – no calls until Thursday 3 PM. You have my word. And sir, I want to assure you that this is purely a temporary operational issue. You have shown willingness to pay and you have the funds. Once the bank lifts the freeze, everything will be resolved. Okay?

Customer: Haan, thank you sir. I appreciate your understanding. Thursday, 3 PM. I will be ready.

Agent: Perfect, Rajesh. Thank you for your cooperation. We will speak on Thursday. Take care.

Agent: Good morning, am I speaking to Rajesh Kumar?

Customer: Haan, yes, this is Rajesh. But I... I have already received a notice from your office, no? The legal notice?

Agent: Yes, Mr. Kumar, I can see that in our system. We sent you a demand notice last month. I'm calling to understand your situation and see if we can work out a solution before this escalates further. You have an outstanding balance of Rs 4,87,500 on your personal loan account ending in 3247. The due date was September 15th.

Customer: Haan, I know, I know about the notice. But see, the thing is... I received summons from the court also. <interruption> The notice said there is legal action starting, and now I have actually received court papers. The case number is there, everything.

Agent: I understand, Mr. Kumar. That's exactly why I'm calling. If we can resolve this now, we can potentially stop the legal proceedings or at least show the court that you are cooperating. Have you had a chance to speak with a lawyer yet?

Customer: Yes, I did. Actually, my brother-in-law, he is a lawyer, and he told me... he said that I should try to settle this before it goes further because court cases are very costly and very lengthy. But the problem is, right now I don't have the full amount. I have been having some issues with my business — the textile business, it is very slow these days.

Agent: I appreciate you sharing that, and I'm glad you're seeking legal advice. That's actually a smart move. What we can do is explore a settlement option that would work for your situation. Given that legal proceedings have started, the settlement may be different from what we might have offered earlier. Can you tell me... what amount do you think you could arrange in the next 30 to 45 days?

Customer: Thirty to forty-five days... that is very tight. My business, we are waiting for some orders from a big client. If those orders come through, maybe I can pay something like Rs 2,50,000 in the next six weeks. But if they don't come, then... <pause> then I cannot promise anything.

Agent: Okay, so Rs 2,50,000 in six weeks is a possibility if your business picks up. That's helpful to know. Now, the legal team will need to be involved in any settlement we discuss because the matter is already in court. What I can do is escalate your case and your offer to our legal department, and they will evaluate whether a settlement structure can be arranged. Does that sound acceptable?

Customer: Yes, yes, that would be good. I don't want to fight in court, yaar. I want to settle this. But I need to be honest — I cannot pay the full amount right now. And my lawyer also said that I should not commit to anything without knowing what the settlement amount would be. So can you tell me... what would be the settlement figure that you are offering?

Agent: That's a very fair point, and your lawyer is right. Given that the matter is now in legal proceedings, I cannot quote you a final settlement figure on this call — that decision has to come from our legal team. What I will do is escalate your willingness to settle and your proposed payment capacity of Rs 2,50,000 within six weeks to our legal department. They will review the case, the court status, and your offer, and they will reach out to you within 3 to 5 working days with a formal settlement proposal. Is that acceptable?

Customer: Okay, okay. So they will call me with the figure?

Agent: Yes, exactly. Our legal team will contact you directly. In the meantime, please ensure you have a conversation with your lawyer about the settlement approach, and also do your best to arrange that Rs 2,50,000 you mentioned. Have you received the court summons documents? Do you understand what you need to do in response?

Customer: I received the papers only yesterday. I haven't read everything carefully yet. My brother-in-law said he will help me with the response. So I should wait for your legal team to call?

Agent: Yes, that's right. Wait for our legal team. In the meantime, do respond to the court through your lawyer if there is a deadline for response — don't ignore the court papers. Our legal team will coordinate with you on the settlement. I'm going to note on your account that you have acknowledged the legal proceedings, that you are open to a settlement, and that you can potentially arrange Rs 2,50,000 within six weeks. Is there any other contact number where the legal team can reach you? The same number we have on file?

Customer: The same number is fine. But can they call after 6 PM? I prefer evening calls because I am usually in the shop in the morning.

Agent: Absolutely, we'll make a note of that. Evening calls only. I am now escalating your case to our legal department with high priority. They will reach out to you within the next 3 to 5 working days with a settlement proposal. Thank you for being cooperative and transparent about your situation, Mr. Kumar. This is the best path forward.

Customer: Okay, thank you. I hope they call soon because I want to resolve this before the court case becomes bigger. Thank you.

Agent: You're welcome, Mr. Kumar. We will be in touch soon through our legal team. Have a good day.

Customer: Yes, yes, that is correct. The same cheque. The amount is fifteen thousand, and now I have the balance. I can even give you an updated cheque if you want, but I prefer to re-present the original one because <interruption> sorry, because the original one is already processed in my records.

Agent: I understand. And you're aware that the bounce fee of two hundred rupees will remain on the account, correct? That's the bank's penalty for the returned cheque.

Customer: Haan, haan, I understand. Two hundred rupees, that's fine. I accept. I just want to clear this and not have any issues with my credit report, you understand? I have plans to take another loan next year for my daughter's education.

Agent: Absolutely, Rajesh, I completely understand. So let me confirm once more: you agree to re-present the original cheque for fifteen thousand rupees, and you acknowledge the two hundred rupee bounce fee. When would you like to re-present the cheque? Can you do it this week?

Customer: No, no, it will clear. I'm sure. My salary came on time last month and this month as well. So there's no issue. I will re-present the cheque on Thursday.

Agent: Excellent, Rajesh. Let me summarize: You agree to re-present the original cheque for fifteen thousand rupees on or before Thursday, the 22nd of this month. The bounce fee of two hundred rupees remains on your account. You understand that if it bounces again, another fee will apply. Is that correct?

Customer: Yes, yes, that is 100% correct. I agree to all of that. Thank you for working with me on this.

Agent: Thank you for your cooperation, Rajesh. I'm going to note this in your account and schedule an internal re-presentation. You should receive a confirmation SMS within two hours. If you have any issues at the bank, please call us back immediately. Is there anything else I can help you with today?

Customer: I did, actually. Same thing happened. Then I thought, let me try the UPI app instead. I have the money, I want to pay, but the system is just not working.

Customer: Yes, definitely. My salary came in on the 10th. I've got enough to pay the EMI and everything else. It's just that the payment gateway is not cooperating. I checked with my bank's customer service as well, and they said their system is fine on their end, so it must be something with the payment gateway on your end or maybe a network connectivity issue.

Agent: Okay, that's very helpful information. So the issue is not on your side — it's a technical failure on the payment infrastructure. Let me note this down. You have the funds, you have the intent, but the digital channels are failing.

Customer: Exactly. I was getting really worried because I didn't want this to affect my credit score or anything. But I knew I couldn't do anything about it last night, so I decided to wait and see if I could call you this morning.

Agent: That was the right call, Priya. Thank you for being proactive. Now, let me help you resolve this. Since the online gateways are not working for you at the moment, do you have an alternate way you could make this payment? For example, we can arrange a direct bank transfer via NEFT or IMPS from the bank branch itself, or you could deposit a cheque or cash at our collection branch if there's one near you.

Customer: A cheque would actually work. I can write a cheque and deposit it at your branch. Where is the nearest one to me? I'm in Bangalore, in Whitefield.

Customer: Yes, I'll do it today if I can, or definitely by tomorrow. I promise.

Agent: Perfect. I'm going to note this down in your account. In the meantime, let me also try to investigate the UPI and NEFT gateway issue on our end. It's possible there was a temporary outage this morning that might have now been resolved. So when would you like to retry the online payment? Or are you confident the cheque route is your preferred option now?

Customer: I think the cheque is safer at this point. I don't want to waste more time on the online stuff if it's going to fail again. But if the gateway is fixed by tomorrow, I could also try NEFT again from the branch itself or from my home computer. Just to have a backup.

Agent: I completely understand, Priya. Your account shows a clean payment history, so this is clearly just a technical issue, not a behavioral one. We'll get this sorted.
